items.summary: देश में एक तरफ जहां चुनाव आयोग की ओर से जारी विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण प्रक्रिया (एसआईआर) को निरस्त करने और मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त के गिरफ्तारी की मांग उठ रही रही है तो वहीं दूसरी तरफ राजधानी दिल्ली में लाखों मतदाता एक दूसरे फेर में फंसे हैं. ये लोग दिल्ली के उन 33 लाख मतदाताओं मे से हैं, जिन्हें चुनाव आयोग की तरफ से नोटिस जारी किया गया है. यह नोटिस दिल्ली के उन वोटरो को दिया है, जो एसआईआर की ड्राफ्ट लिस्ट मे जगह नहीं बना पाए. वहीं, अब अंतिम मतदाता सूची मे अपना नाम जुड़वाने के लिए दस्तावेज लेकर मतदाता केंद्रों के बाहर घंटो कतार में खड़े इंतजार कर रहे हैं. हमने इस प्रक्रिया की जमीनी हकीकत समझने के लिए दिल्ली के ऐसे ही दो मतदाता केंद्रों का दौरा किया. अपनी पड़ताल में हमने पाया कि इनमें से अधिकतर लोग काम से छुट्टी लेकर आए हैं. वहीं, दिहाड़ीदार मजदूर इस प्रक्रिया से नाराज दिखे क्योंकि इसके चलते उनकी हर रोज की दिहाड़ी का नुकसान हो रहा है. कोंडली के रहने वाले संदीप कुमार ने बताया कि वह 700 रुपए दिहाड़ी पर काम करते हैं लेकिन एसआईआर की वजह से उन्हें दिहाड़ी छोड़नी पड़ी. अपनी परेशानी बताते समय वह कहते हैं, “एक दिन की दिहाड़ी छूटने से महीने का बजट गड़बड़ा जाता है. आज मेरा सात सौ का नुकसान हो गया. अगर आज काम पर जाता तो पांच सौ रुपये और जोड़कर गैस सिलेंडर आ जाता जो महीने भर चलता.” इसी तरह बुराड़ी के 52 वर्षीय राजेश बताते हैं कि वह मतदाता केंद्र का चक्कर लगाकर हताश हो चुके हैं. वह कहते हैं, “इस उत्पीड़न से तो अच्छा है सरकार हमें दूसरे देश का नागरिक ही घोषित कर दे. मैं दिल्ली में तीस साल से वोट कर रहा हूं लेकिन आज मुझे सबूत देना पड़ रहा है कि मै वोटर हूं या नहीं.” वहीं, इस प्रासेस पर सवाल उठाते हुए शबीना कहती हैं, “मुझे समझ में नही आता कि वह कौन सा ऐसा दस्तावेज होगा, जिसे दिखाकर बता पाएं कि हम इसी देश के नागरिक हैं.” देखिए हमारी ये खास रिपोर्ट. बुराड़ी में एसआईआर का असर, 1 लाख 67 हजार लोगों के नाम वोटर लिस्ट से बाहर एसआईआर कैंप: सवालों और संशय के बीच कैसे तैयार हो रही मतदाताओं की सूची

items.title: Karnataka High Court stays forgery case against cult.fit co-founder Rishabh Telang
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday stayed the investigation in criminal proceedings initiated against fitness platform Cult.fit's co-founder Rishabh Telang on allegations of cheating, forgery and criminal breach of trust, among others [Rishabh Telang v. State of Karnataka]. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde granted the interim stay on investigation and will hear the matter on September 30. "Since the matter is heard on merits, further investigation is stayed till the next date of hearing." Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Telang’s brother-in-law and Cult co-founder Deepak Poduval accusing him of forging documents connected to the transfer of the original Cult business and the subsequent closure of Cult Fitness Private Limited. Bellandur Police lodged an FIR against Telang on August 6. Poduval alleged that he and Telang incorporated Cult Fitness in November 2015 as its only two subscribers, with each holding a 50 per cent stake. According to the complaint, Telang subsequently excluded him from the management of the company and diverted its business, customers, goodwill and revenue to Cultfit Healthcare Private Limited, which was incorporated in August 2016. Poduval further alleged that his signatures were forged on financial statements and documents submitted to the Registrar of Companies to have Cult Fitness struck off in 2019. He claimed that he discovered the alleged irregularities only after examining the company’s records in May and June 2026. The FIR invoked provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy, along with Section 66D of the Information Technology Act. Senior Advocate Sandesh Chouta , appearing for Telang, submitted the dispute is a commercial in nature and that criminal proceedings have been initiated to harass his client. Senior Advocate Sandesh J Chouta Chouta was assisted by Advocates Mohammed Shakeeb, Chetan Tayal and Sathies Kumar from Multi State Collaborative Legal. Advocate Ahaan Mohan appeared for Poduval. [Read Order]

items.title: Karnataka High Court forms 3-judge panel to assess feasibility of more HC benches
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday constituted a three-member committee to examine the feasibility of establishing circuit or permanent benches of High Court at Mangaluru, Udupi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu-Madikeri, Hassan, Davanagere and Uttara Kannada. The committee was constituted by the Chief Justice through a notification dated September 29. The three-member panel comprises Justice Anu Sivaraman , Justice SG Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz . Justice Anu Sivaraman, Justice S G Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz The notification states that the committee has been constituted to verify the feasibility of establishing a High Court circuit bench/permanent bench in the identified regions. The committee has also been directed to consult all stakeholders before submitting its report to the High Court on the feasibility of establishing such benches. The notification, issued by Registrar General M Chandrashekar Reddy, states that the committee will function with immediate effect. The issue assumes significance since Karnataka currently has the principal seat at Bengaluru and benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi. The proposal for an additional bench at Mangaluru had earlier triggered a debate within the legal fraternity, with proponents citing the need to improve access to justice for litigants from distant parts of the State. On May 13, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had written to Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru seeking consideration of the proposal for establishing a circuit bench at Mangaluru and assuring the State government's cooperation in implementing the proposal. The State government had also identified the old Deputy Commissioner's office in Mangaluru as potential infrastructure for the proposed bench. The May proposal stated that around 50,000 square feet of space could be repurposed for court operations and also said that residential accommodation for judges have been identified. The proposal, however, faced opposition from the Advocates' Association Bengaluru (AAB). In a memorandum dated May 18 addressed to Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru, the AAB opposed the proposed Mangaluru bench and contended that any decision taken without stakeholder consultation and an empirical or statistical study on the necessity of a new bench would be premature. items.title: RTE quota in private schools: Supreme Court pulls up NCPCR for indifference, asks chairperson to appear
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday pulled up the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) over its approach towards implementing the 25 percent reservation for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in private unaided schools under the Right to Education Act [Dinesh Biwaji Ashtikar v. State of Maharashtra] A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which the child rights body had responded to the issue. “How can they act so indifferent? Who heads the NCPCR? We will ask that officer to be present at the next hearing. This is not a contempt proceeding. We asked them to collate, but it is not a question of merely collating. They will have to address the purpose of Section 12 and ensure that every neighbourhood school implements the concept,” the Court said. It thus asked the Chairperson and Director of the NCPCR to remain present before the Court at the next hearing. The Supreme Court has been monitoring the implementation of this provision across the country. In a judgment delivered in January this year, the Court had stressed that the 25 percent requirement was not merely aimed at providing free education to children from weaker and disadvantaged sections, but also at promoting social integration by enabling children from different socio-economic backgrounds to study together in neighbourhood schools. As part of that exercise, the Court had impleaded the NCPCR for compliance and monitoring and directed it to collect information on rules and regulations issued by States and Union Territories (UTs) for implementing the provision. items.title: Karnataka High Court grants ₹2.77 crore to man paralysed after tree branch fell on him; calls for use of AI to identify hazards
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently directed civic authorities to pay ₹2.77 crore with 6% interest to a Bengaluru resident who suffered permanent paraplegia after a branch of a Gulmohar tree fell on him while he was walking on a public road [Chandan G v. State of Karnataka]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj held that the BBMP (now Greater Bengaluru Authority) owed a statutory and public duty in relation to the tree even though it stood within the premises of a private school. The Court also found that the civic body had actual notice of the danger at least from February 22, 2024, before the incident that occured on March 7, 2024., Justice Suraj Govindraj It also called upon the State government to establish a mechanism by which a public safety hazard, once reported or detected, is addressed despite the responsibility being divided among different departments, authorities, contractors, utilities or private owners. "The object is to ensure that once a danger is brought to the notice of the competent authority, or is otherwise reasonably identified, the information is recorded, assessed according to the degree of risk, entrusted to a named person or authority and followed through until the danger is made safe and the remedial work is independently verified," it said. The Court thus issued a slew of guidelines including use of cameras and artificial intelligence (AI) to detect public safety hazards, maintenance of digital records, time-bound response depending on the level of threat, recurrence monitoring, preventive maintenance, periodic inspection etc. The petitioner suffered a severe spinal injury after a branch of a Gulmohar tree from the premises of Good Shepherd Convent School fell on him while he was walking to work. He underwent spinal decompression, stabilisation surgery and prolonged rehabilitation. His disability was assessed at 85%, while the Court treated his functional disability as 100% for calculating loss of future earning capacity. The Court assessed total compensation at ₹2,82,29,695, including ₹24,44,271 towards medical expenses, ₹1,03,85,424 towards loss of future earning capacity, ₹27 lakh towards attendant and care charges, ₹1.17 crore towards future medical, physiotherapy, massage and rehabilitation expenses, and ₹5 lakh each towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities. items.title: GNLU students protest over health, water and sanitation conditions on campus
items.summary: Students at Gujarat National Law University (GNLU), Gandhinagar are protesting over health, water and sanitation conditions on campus. The students have placed a statement of demands before the University. They have sought responsibility fixed for each lapse, an independent audit of hostel water, food, sanitation and medical conditions, and regular reports shared with students. They have also sought testing of hostel water for E coli and other pathogens. They also want RO or filter facilities on every hostel floor, including the third floor of the academic block. Students say that the medical centre needs more staff and equipment. Only one person is reportedly stationed with the ambulance for 24-hour coverage, which they say is insufficient given the number of students on campus. They have also demanded regular external inspection of the mess, permanent repair of sewage leaks, mosquito control across the hostels and written communication of all decisions. Furthermore, the students want offline classes suspended until the fixes are complete or moved online if that takes over a week. They have asked that internal assessments be held online or rescheduled with no loss of attendance or marks. With end-semester exams about three weeks away, they have also asked for an advance procedure for medical exemptions and a written academic plan. The piece also claims students found worms in water bottles and a blade in rice on August 12. items.title: Supreme Court cancels bail of accused in Chinese investment app money laundering case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday cancelled the bail granted to Bhupesh Arora and rejected the bail plea of his co-accused Rohit Vij in a money laundering case arising from an investigation into alleged fake Chinese-linked investment apps. [Directorate of Enforcement v. Bhupesh Arora] A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale observed that a compromise in the predicate offence would not extinguish the underlying criminal activity. Justice M.M. Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B. Varale The Court was hearing the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) challenge to the Delhi High Court order granting bail to Arora, along with Vij’s plea challenging a separate Delhi High Court order refusing him bail. The case arose from an ED probe into an alleged cyber fraud and money laundering network involving the LOXAM investment app, through which people were allegedly induced to invest money on promises of high returns. The ED registered its case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) on the basis of a predicate offence registered by the Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police after a complainant alleged that he had been cheated of ₹1.16 lakh through the app. According to the ED, money collected through the alleged fraud was routed through several bank and virtual accounts and subsequently converted into cash and foreign currency. The agency alleged that Vij was involved in operating Ranjan Moneycorp Private Limited and KDS Forex Private Limited, which were used to receive and convert the alleged proceeds. As regards Bhupesh Arora, the ED alleged that he controlled a number of entities through which proceeds from cyber fraud were layered. The agency also relied on statements and financial transactions to allege that cash and foreign currency generated through the network were ultimately delivered to Arora and his associates. The Delhi High Court granted bail to Arora in February after finding prima facie gaps in the material linking him to the alleged money laundering. It also took note of the fact that the predicate FIR had been quashed following a compromise. In a separate judgment, the High Court refused bail to Vij in August, distinguishing his case from Arora’s in view of his alleged role in the cash and foreign-exchange conversion mechanism. The ED then moved the Supreme Court against Arora’s bail, while Vij challenged the refusal of bail to him. The Supreme Court heard the matters together and set aside Arora’s bail while dismissing Vij’s plea. Senior Advocate Muk

items.title: Delhi High Court constitutes committee under ex-CJI Sanjiv Khanna to oversee Greenopolis homebuyers’ claims
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday appointed a monitoring committee headed by former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Sanjiv Khanna to oversee and streamline the claims of hundreds of homebuyers affected by the stalled Greenopolis housing project in Gurugram [Directorate of Enforcement v Greenopolis Welfare Confederation and Anr] . Former Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officers HS Sharma and Ajay Kumar Kuhar will assist Justice Khanna in the committee. Justice Khanna has offered to work pro bono. In a detailed order, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani said that the committee will verify genuine homebuyers, assess competing claims over properties attached by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and facilitate restitution to eligible claimants. It asked the Justice Khanna committee to endeavour to complete its work within eight months of its first meeting and submit reports every three months. Anup Jairam Bhambhani The Court passed the order while dealing with petitions by the ED, Greenopolis Welfare Association (GWA) and Greenopolis Welfare Confederation (GWC) challenging the November 27, 2025 PMLA Court order. The dispute concerns the Greenopolis project in Gurugram, developed by Three C Shelters and Orris Infrastructure. Of 1,862 units, 1,650 had been allotted before abandonment. Three C Shelters allegedly collected ₹776.60 crore and Orris collected ₹383.06 crore from homebuyers. The ED argued that ₹214.09 crore was siphoned off to related entities. In its order, the Special Court had ordered restoration and disposal of ED-attached properties. The ED challenged this, citing improper identification of beneficiaries and non-compliance with the statutory framework. After considering the case, the High Court noted that there were several complexities in the case. Therefore, it constituted the monitoring committee. The Court clarified that the committee's proceedings would not interfere with the ongoing corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) or affect homebuyers' rights in those proceedings. items.title: Private hospitals functioning like industries, not service providers: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday criticized the commercialization of private healthcare, observing that corporate hospitals operate as profit-driven industries rather than service providers while common citizens and taxpayers bear the brunt of exorbitant drug markups [ Kishan Chand Jain v. Union of India ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta noted that corporate hospitals compel admitted patients to purchase medicines exclusively from their in-house pharmacies at inflated retail prices, while patients who bring medicines from outside are left high and dry with hospitals refusing to assure treatment. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The hearing comes as a continuation of proceedings from last week, where the top court had flagged a ten-fold price difference in a cancer drug - where the Price to Retailer (PTR) was ₹2,700 but the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) was ₹27,000. At the time, the Court had termed the un-capped markup an "absolute rampage and carnage" and "broad daylight dacoity." ₹2,700 cancer medicine sold for ₹27,000: Supreme Court flags "broad daylight dacoity" of patients During today's hearing, the Bench highlighted that when patients undergo treatment under government-sponsored welfare schemes, corporate hospitals obtain full reimbursement from the exchequer based on these artificially inflated MRPs. "In corporate hospitals... ₹27,000 MRP. PTR is around ₹3,000. Just see the difference. Corporate hospital says you have to buy from our chemist. items.title: Delhi High Court quizzes Meta over Instagram feature being misused to violate copyright
items.summary: The Delhi High Court today raised concerns that a feature on social media platform Instagram could be used as a tool to violate the copyrights of original content creators [ Dr Vikas Divyakirti vs Meta Platforms ]. Addressing counsel representing Meta (which owns Instagram) Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani noted that this feature allows Instagram users to make changes to reels posted by others, and re-upload a modified version. "Tell me Mr Pathak (Meta's counsel), you have a feature on Instagram that you can pick up a video, paste it and make it your own video. For example, someone is cooking a recipe, you can take the whole video and add yourself cooking as per the recipe and run it on your own handle," the Court observed. The Court stated that this Instagram feature allows manipulation and enables copyright infringement. "You are allowing manipulation. It is a tool for copyright violation. Does your platform permit this? It is proof of copyright violation. It is a mischievous feature you have got there. These are powerful tools you are creating; then you give these to a ghost. You don't know who is going to use these tools. In our country today, if one has to own a gun they will be put to whole (application and approval process)…This is worse than a gun," Justice Bhambhani stated. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani Advocate Varun Pathak, representing Meta, stated that he will look into the concerns raised by the Court. The Court was possibly referring to Instagram's “remix” feature, which allows users to create a new reel using an existing public reel or video. This feature lets users add their own recorded or pre-recorded video alongside the original content, allowing them to respond to, recreate or demonstrate something shown in the original video while posting the remix on their own Instagram handle. The original creator and content remain identifiable as part of the remix. Concerns about the possible misuse of such features were raised by the Court today while hearing a suit filed by educator and founder of Drishti IAS coaching centre, Vikas Divyakirti, who has sought the protection of his personality rights. items.title: Ten years on, still struggling to execute foreign arbitral award: Daiichi tells Supreme Court
items.summary: Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that nearly ten years after securing a foreign arbitral award against former Ranbaxy promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh, it was still struggling to execute the award [Yes Bank Vs Daiichi Sankyo]. Senior Advocate Arvind Datar , appearing for Daiichi, said the company had pursued arbitration, obtained an award on April 29, 2016 and then initiated execution proceedings, but was yet to realise the award. " It’s 10 years to execute an award, international award ,” Datar said. He added that the situation has become a “spider’s web”, with disputes continuing over what happened to shares of Fortis Healthcare Limited (FHL) held by the judgment debtors. Supreme Court, Arvind Datar The submissions were made before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of challenges by banks and financial institutions to the Delhi High Court’s directions for a forensic audit in the execution proceedings initiated by Daiichi. Datar told the Court that the banks and the judgment debtors have taken conflicting stands on whether certain Fortis shares were encumbered, who invoked the pledges and who ultimately sold the shares. “The banks blame the judgment-debtors, judgment-debtors blame the bank, and I am the decree-holder, I am not getting any relief at all, ” he submitted. Datar also explained why Daiichi had earlier stated that it did not want to pursue a forensic audit against the banks. He said there were 17 banks involved and that Daiichi had taken the stand out of “sheer frustration”, since hearing every bank separately would further prolong the execution proceedings. Daiichi had therefore asked that the forensic exercise proceed “once and for all”. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The banks, on the other hand, argued that they were neither judgment debtors nor garnishees and that some of them were themselves owed money by the judgment debtors or their group entities. Senior Advocate Shyam Divan argued that opening up the books of a bank to a third-party forensic auditor would have serious consequences, particularly when Daiichi itself had ultimately said that it did not want a forensic audit of the banks. items.title: Juniors lawyers must be paid stipend: Madhya Pradesh High Court orders State Bar Council to frame guidelines
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has issued directions to ensure that junior advocates are paid a stipend for their work [Vipin Pandey v. Rani Durgavati University, Jabalpur & Ors.]. Justice Vishal Dhagat said that the bar body should ensure that young lawyers' ability to maintain a decent standard of living and have their transportation expenses covered during the initial phases of law practice. Hence, it directed the Madhya Pradesh State Bar Council to consult the High Court Bar Association and the High Court Advocates' Bar Association to formulate guidelines setting a minimum stipend for junior advocates across urban and rural areas within a strict six-month timeframe. The order was passed during the hearing of a petition where a junior counsel, appearing for the petitioner, sought an adjournment on the ground that the arguing counsel was not available. Upon being questioned by the Court, the junior counsel revealed that she was not receiving any stipend. Taking serious note of the disclosure, Justice Dhagat referred to the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) circular dated October 15, 2024, which recommended a minimum monthly stipend of ₹20,000 in urban areas and ₹15,000 in rural areas for junior advocates for at least three years from the date of enrolment Justice Vishal Dhagat While noting that the BCI circular is recommendatory in nature, the High Court stressed that the State Bar Council must step in to make financial support workable on the ground: "State Bar Council being regulatory body is having heavy burden to see that junior advocates are paid stipend for maintaining their expenses and transportation. Decision in this regard be taken within a limited time frame of six months for issuing guidelines through Bar Association in State of Madhya Pradesh," the Court said. The Bench further directed the State Bar Council to conduct an inquiry into why advocates Rajesh Dubey, Aniruddh Kumar Mishra, Chandrika Prasad Dwivedi, Dhananjay Chaturvedi and Naveen Kumar Pathak were not paying a stipend to the junior counsel appearing in the matter. "The operation of hookah bars and the rendering of hookah services by the restaurants within the State of Uttar Pradesh constitutes a flagrant violation of Rule 4(3) of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008 as amended in 2017 and is in direct contravention of the scheme and object of COTPA," the Court ruled. items.title: No fear of animal cruelty law because of low fines: J&K High Court calls for heavier penalties, jail time
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh recently called for stricter jail time and heavier penalties for offences under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 [Anwar Jan v. Union Territory of J&K] . The Bench observed that animals experience pain, stress and fear like humans, while noting that the existing legal framework continues to treat animals largely as objects or property. It also expressed concern over the penalties prescribed under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, observing that fines for certain acts of cruelty can be as low as ₹10 to ₹50. "Since these fines are so low, there is almost no fear of the law, which is why we see people committing acts of abuse just to post videos on social media for views. While the courts have agreed that animals deserve to live without suffering, the written law has not changed enough yet. For real change to happen, the law needs to officially recognize the animal feelings and replace those tiny fines with strict jail time and heavy penalties,” the Court observed. A Division Bench of Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani made the observations while allowing an appeal against the dismissal of a habeas corpus petition filed by Anwar Jan (Choudhary), who had been detained under the Jammu & Kashmir Public Safety Act, 1978. Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani The record showed that Jan had been involved in several criminal cases and was also accused in multiple bovine-smuggling cases. He had previously faced PSA detention as well. The Court said that bovine animal smuggling is not merely a criminal offence but can also hurt religious sentiments and has the potential to disturb public tranquillity. However, it clarified that even in such cases, authorities must strictly comply with the constitutional safeguards governing preventive detention. The Division Bench found several serious defects in the latest detention order. It noted that the appellant was already in custody but the detention order did not demonstrate awareness of his custody or record any compelling reason showing a real possibility of his release and subsequent involvement in prejudicial activities. items.title: Delhi High Court sets aside FSSAI order directing Red Bull to drop ‘Energy Drink’ label

Justice Amit Mahajan found that the company had not been given an opportunity to respond before the FSSAI direction was issued. “ It remains undisputed that the order dated 30th June, 2026 directing the petitioner to not use the term ‘Energy Drink’ in its product was passed without affording any opportunity to the petitioner to file any reply or give any explanation ,” the Court observed. The Court, therefore, allowed Red Bull’s petition challenging the FSSAI's June 30 order, on the limited ground that natural justice principles had been violated. Red Bull had also relied on a March 2024 FSSAI advisory which, according to the petition, permitted the expression “Energy Drink” for products falling under the relevant food categories. items.title: Bombay HC asks sessions court to reconsider plea to close POCSO case against accused with mental incapacity
items.summary: The Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court recently quashed a sessions court order that had refused to discharge a 19-year-old accused in a POCSO case, despite medical evidence establishing his mental incapacity to face criminal trial. Justice Mehroz K Pathan remanded the matter back to the Additional Sessions Court in Bhandara district of Maharashtra for fresh consideration. Justice Mehroz K Pathan The accused faced prosecution for offences under the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). His lawyers filed a plea to discharge him from the case, claiming that he suffered from severe intellectual vulnerability. They argued that he could not comprehend his actions or instruct counsel. Medical tests, including a psychiatric assessment, revealed that the accused had an Intelligence Quotient below seventy and a mental age of approximately fourteen. Three doctors subsequently testified before the trial court confirming that the accused suffered from mild intellectual disability and was unfit to stand trial. However, the additional sessions judge rejected the discharge plea in August 2025. The trial judge found the medical experts lacked a uniform opinion. A plea was then moved on behalf of the accused before the High Court, challenging this trial court decision. items.title: Kunal Kamra moves Supreme Court in 7-judge bench case on limits of legislative privileges
items.summary: Comedian Kunal Kamra has approached the Supreme Court seeking to intervene in a case pending before a seven-judge Bench of the Court on the extent to which an exercise of legislative privileges can be used to curtail a citizen’s freedom of speech. Kamra has sought permission to be made party in the case of N Ravi and ors v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai , in which the Court is slated to examine the interplay of legislative privileges with the freedom of speech and the right to life and liberty. Kamra was prompted to move his plea for intervention on account of the breach of privilege proceedings that he presently faces before the Maharashtra assembly over a satirical song played on his comedy show ‘Naya Bharat.’ Kamra’s satirical performance dwelt on the split of the Shiv Sena party in 2022, which led to the resignation of then Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, and the eventual formation of a new State regime led by Eknath Shinde. In his song, Kamra also reportedly called Shinde ‘Gaddar’ (traitor). Due to this, he faced breach of privilege proceedings before the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly on grounds that he disrespected and insulted Shinde. A criminal case was also registered against him. Kamra has already filed a plea to quash the criminal case before the Bombay High Court, which stayed his arrest but is yet to give its final verdict in the matter. Kamra has now sought to make submissions before the Supreme Court on the larger issue of the limits of legislative privilege. “The Applicant believes that his case demonstrates that the exercise of legislative privileges affects not only the freedom of speech and expression of members of the press, but also of any citizen who wishes to speak about the actions of members of the legislature,” his plea states. He goes on to argue that if legislative privilege is invoked in this manner, it would have a chilling effect on the free speech of citizens across India. items.title: Sambhal violence: Supreme Court quashes NSA detention of Mulla Afroz, imposes ₹10 lakh costs on UP
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday quashed the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Mulla Afroz, accused of being the alleged mastermind of the 2024 Sambhal violence [Mulla Afroz v. Union of India & Ors.] . A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu held that an alleged confessional statement cannot be the sole ground for preventive detention. "Confessional statement cannot be the sole ground for detention, surrounding circumstances have to be looked into," said the Court. The Court found that the detaining authority had failed to take into consideration appropriate material before passing the detention order. “In fact, whatever has been said by the detaining authority has been discussed to hold that the power of detention has been illegally exercised,” it said. The Court accordingly allowed Afroz's appeal and quashed the detention order, the confirmation order and the Allahabad High Court judgment upholding his detention. Additionally, it also imposed costs of ₹10 lakh on the State of Uttar Pradesh. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu The case arose from the violence that broke out in Sambhal in November 2024, following a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid. Four people were killed in the violence. Afroz was arrested around 54 days after the incident and was subsequently granted bail by the Allahabad High Court. The Sambhal District Magistrate, however, passed an order on October 13, 2025 directing Afroz's preventive detention under Section 3 of the NSA. The order was subsequently upheld by the Allahabad High Court, following which Afroz approached the Supreme Court. Before the Supreme Court, Afroz challenged the material relied upon for his detention, including an alleged confessional statement made in police custody. The Court questioned the State on whether such a confession could form the basis of the detaining authority's satisfaction under the NSA. items.title: Justice Dipankar Datta pays tribute to his late law clerk in judgment
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta on Tuesday began one of his judgments by paying tribute to his young law clerk who passed away four days ago. In a judgment delivered in relation to the Sambhal violence case, the Court acknowledged the research and work put in by law clerk-cum-research associate Ritwik Deswal, who expired four days before his 27th birthday. "The order is in memoriam. Human life is fragile, yet in the ordinary course of living, we seldom pause to recognise just how fleeting it is. And when life finally confronts us with that fragility, the realisation often comes too late. On that note, at the very outset, we begin on an unconventional premise. One of our dearest law clerks-cum research associates, Ritwik Deswal, left for his heavenly abode, four days short of his 27th birthday, which happens to be today. As we pronounce this judgment, which bears the quiet and indelible imprint of his final labors, we hasten to record our deep appreciation for the invaluable research assistance rendered by him in the build-up to the preparation of this judgment. His untimely demise has left an excruciatingly deep void in our lives. Even in his final hours, his thoughts remained firmly anchored in the pursuit of truth and the service of justice. It is therefore with profound personal sorrow and grief that we dedicate this final collaboration to his memory, his integrity, his indomitable commitment to the law, his love for academia, and his other great qualities of head and heart," the Court said in the very first paragraph of the judgment. The plea was mentioned before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant by Senior Advocate Vikas Singh . "The purpose of having a multi-member Commission was that, and the statute says so, that it has to be a decision unanimously or by majority. Now, the way the Election Commission has functioned, there is serious doubt about whether there was a decision of the Election Commission for this entire exercise of special intensive revision. Because if the Commission has not taken a unanimous decision, then this... What the Court has also decided is on the basis that it is a Commission's decision. So it is a serious issue," Singh said. "List it next week," the CJI directed. The plea has sought a writ of Quo Warranto asking the CEC to explain under what authority he has acted, and continues to act, as though entitled individually to exercise the collective decision-making power vested by Article 324 of the Constitution in the Election Commission as a body. The ECI comprises the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners. Currently, Gyanesh Kumar serves as CEC while Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi are the two ECs. Whenever, there is no unanimity among the three, decisions have to be arrived at based on majority. However, according to recent reports by the Indian Express, the ECI took various decisions despite two Elections Commissioners not agreeing to the same. The petition before the Court, filed by one Rakesh Kumar Singh, has alleged “progressive centralisation” of power, absence/delay of agendas and minutes, changes to electoral-roll processes and filing of appeals without the two Election Commissioners’ knowledge or approval. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed a criminal case filed against a YouTuber, Prathap NM, popularly known as 'Drone Prathap', who was booked for causing an explosion in an artificial pond using 100 grams of sodium as part of a science experiment [ Pratap NM v State of Karnataka ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj noted that the experiment formed a part of the 10th standard NCERT syllabus and the YouTuber appeared to have made his video for educational purposes. The judge added that since Prathap had not demonstrated any malicious intent, there was no need to prosecute him for criminal offences, including offences under the Explosive Substances Act, 1908. "This Court does not condone or commend the acts taken by the petitioner. (However) the fact remains it is not a malicious action but only an educative action on part of the petitioner which would not require such educator to go through the ignominy of an investigation and a criminal trial thereafter," the Court said. Justice Suraj Govindaraj Prathap had been booked in the case after he dropped 100 grams of sodium into an artificial pond to create an explosion as part of a science experiment. A video he uploaded on YouTube of the experiment went viral on social media, leading to his arrest in December 2024. He was booked for the offence of causing an explosion likely to endanger life or property under Section 3 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, and negligent conduct with respect to explosive substances under Section 288 of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. He was later granted bail. He also deleted the controversial video. He eventually moved the High Court with a plea to quash the first information report (FIR) filed against him. His counsel told the Court that the experiment was conducted on an artificial pond created at his friend's private farm, and that all safety precautions were taken. The Court factored in that the YouTuber was an educator and content creator who had built 600 drones from electronic waste. The Court further observed that Pratap had used his video to demonstrate a chemical reaction for educational purposes. The Court further noted that the YouTuber had made no attempt to suppress evidence of the explosion and had uploaded the video for public viewing. items.title: Progress in women safety post Nirbhaya questionable: Supreme Court orders vulnerable-area mapping, more CCTVs, lighting, police patrol
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday issued a slew of directions aimed at improving safety in public spaces across Delhi-NCR in its suo motu case concerning a series of rape cases in the region, including the alleged gang rape of a teenager at a public park [In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran expressed concern over what it described as systemic failures on the part of law enforcement and civil authorities to ensure basic public safety. That morning, a two Judge bench of the Supreme Court placed before the Chief Justice of India the issue on whether a Constitution Bench reference is merited with respect to a challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 (2023 Act) .
